findings.claim: The round-2 repair introduced a blind-solvable seam between key B and distractor C (shared agent + absolutised sibling), and the pedagogy record clears the repaired unit as a bare SOUND while the same round's G-STEM records a MAJOR construct-validity finding with blind_pick = B. The unit's own construct-validity paragraph covers only length and hedging, never this seam.
findings.evidence: verdicts/verdicts-gstem.jsonl (current round) on q:1, verdict 'flag', severity major: "PARTIALLY (blind_pick B). C logically entails B (\"two thirds of them came soon after a tamping machine had been through\"): if all buckles fell within eight weeks of tamping, then two thirds came soon after tamping. Under a single-key convention the stronger option cannot be the unique answer, so a reader with zero domain knowledge eliminates C by pure logic and is left leaning to the surviving quantified sibling. Still 3-way undecided against A and D, so flag, not kill." The seam is repair-introduced: verdicts-round1/verdicts-gstem.jsonl records G-STEM 'pass', findings [] on the pre-repair option set, where B read "That two thirds of them came soon after a gang had worked the ballast." (repair_log round 2, MINOR-3 edit). The shipped rationale frames the tightened pair as a feature rather than a risk: "C and the key now name the same agent, so the quantifier is the only thing that decides between them, which is exactly the reading the item is testing", and its construct-validity sentence addresses only two heuristics: "neither 'pick the qualified answer' nor 'strip the absolutes' locates the key." report.json/elf-b15-003 ships the unit as "status": "SURVIVED_FLAGGED" with this flag open; reviews/pedagogy.jsonl carries "verdict":"SOUND" with no note.
findings.why: Probe 4 of pedagogy-review is exactly "Can a test-wise student score without reading?" and its output contract mandates a construct_validity line naming "any blind-solvable tell"; a bare SOUND asserts none while a same-round gate documents one on that precise axis, so the correct verdict was MINOR_FIXES with the tell named. Held to minor rather than a refutation because (a) the gate itself judged it flag-not-kill and reports the blind reader still "3-way undecided", (b) the entailment needs the pedantic 'at least' reading of "two thirds" — under the ordinary exact reading B and C are mutually exclusive, not nested, (c) option A also concerns ballast work, which dilutes the two-option convergence signal, (d) all seven batch15 review lines are terse verdict-only records with no findings array, so the missing construct_validity line is a logging-format artifact and cannot by itself prove the stage failed to consider the seam, and (e) the flag is on the shipped record, so no information is lost downstream. Cheapest closure is one rationale sentence acknowledging the C-entails-B path (rationale-only, no re-gate); de-tightening C would require a G-KEY/G-DISTRACTOR re-gate and is not warranted for a flag the gate declined to kill.

findings.claim: A rationale clause attributes to the passage a proportion the passage never states.
findings.evidence: Rationale (C paragraph): "A third of the logged buckles fell outside that window, which is precisely the proportion the passage is careful to state." The nearest antecedent of "which" is "A third", and the passage never states a third: its only proportion is "two in three came in the eight weeks after ballast work". Neither "a third" nor "one in three" occurs anywhere in the passage.
findings.why: Probe 3 (rationale factual accuracy) treats every claim in the teaching payload as a claim to verify. The arithmetic is sound — 39 buckles, two in three = 26 in window, 13 (exactly one third) outside — and the complement is trivially derivable, so nothing false is taught; it is an attribution slip fixable with three words ("which is the complement of the proportion the passage is careful to state"). Minor, no re-gate.

findings.claim: The D paragraph names the tally as the sentence that disqualifies D, but the tally is logically compatible with D; the round-2 repair demoted the sentence that actually cuts against it.
findings.evidence: Rationale: "the disqualifier that does the work is the tally itself, which is the log's own answer to when the buckles came - two in three of them in the eight weeks after ballast work - so D substitutes a clustering the record does not report." Two in three falling in the eight weeks after ballast work does not exclude those same eight-week windows from being the district's hottest weeks, so the tally alone leaves D ("That most of them fell in the hottest weeks the district has on record.") standing. The directly counter-evidential sentence is "The hottest week on record produced none.", which the round-2 repair downgraded to "cuts against" while adding "a single week is thin ground from which to refute a claim about weeks in the plural".
findings.why: Round 2 closed round-1's MINOR-1 over-claim ('contradicts') by installing a differently overstated one (a compatible fact promoted to 'the disqualifier that does the work'). It stays minor because the genuinely correct reason is stated in the same paragraph - "the log simply never says this" and "D substitutes a clustering the record does not report" - against a prompt that asks what we are told, so a student reading the rationale is not taught anything false. Fix is one clause, no re-gate.
